fn.en: Say what is necessary, what isn’t, what is allowed and what isn’t.

items.s: Our teacher was very ___ — nobody spoke without permission. ⚖️
You have to pass an ___ to get into that university. 📝
It’s free and it’s local: a ___. 🏫
I got a good ___ in maths and a terrible one in art. 🅰️
She wants to ___ as a nurse. 🎓
Leaving that course was the best ___ I ever made. 🤔

items.a: You have to wear a uniform at this school
You don’t have to pay — it’s a state school
You’re not allowed to use your phone in class
You can leave after the last lesson
I must remember to send that form
Do you have to take an entrance exam

sub.en: Look at the sentences. Which one is somebody else’s rule, and which one is your own idea?

items.q: It’s the school rule: you ___ wear a uniform.
items.why: have to = a rule from outside — the school, the law, the boss. must = usually your own feeling that something is necessary.

items.q: Nobody is making me: I ___ remember to send that form.

items.why: don’t have to = it isn’t necessary. mustn’t = it is forbidden. These two are opposites, not the same.

items.q: It is forbidden: you ___ use your phone in class.
It is permitted: you ___ leave after the last lesson.
It is forbidden, said more gently: you ___ to use your phone.
___ you have to take an entrance exam?
She ___ read a map at six, but she had to be shown twice.

use: One day I was telling him…
It’s one of the first words I learnt.
tts: Then one day I was telling him all the new words we’d learnt that day in class.
Snow — because I like the quiet snow world. It’s white and clean and I love freezing weather.
It’s one of the first words that I learnt in English.
It seems full of possibilities leading to a bright future.
It’s a very short and simple word but it means a lot.
It makes me think of young flowers and crisp, sunny spring mornings.

short and simple but meaning a lot

items.q: One word makes a speaker think of

acts.title: The classroom that worked
text: I have been in three schools and only one of them worked, and I have spent years trying to say why.
It wasn’t the money. It was a state school and you didn’t have to pay for anything except the trips. It wasn’t the building, which leaked.

The rules were unusual. You had to be on time, and that was enforced absolutely — the door was locked at nine. But you didn’t have to put your hand up, you didn’t have to ask to leave the room, and you weren’t allowed to say “I don’t know” and stop there. You had to say what you did know first.

One teacher had a rule I have never seen anywhere else: you could ask any question, but you weren’t allowed to ask it twice without trying to answer it yourself in between. It sounds strict. It felt like being taken seriously.
The results were good, but that isn’t the part I remember. I remember that nobody was ever bored, and I have not been able to explain that to anybody who wasn’t there.

items.s: You had to pay for the trips.
You had to be on time.
You had to put your hand up.
You were allowed to say “I don’t know” and stop.
The writer says nobody was ever bored.

write.q: Describe the rules of your school or your workplace: 6 sentences. Two things you have to do, two you don’t have to do, one you aren’t allowed to do, and one you can do freely.
write.ph: At my school you have to…
write.model: At my old school you had to be on time — the door was locked at nine and that was the end of the discussion. You had to wear a uniform, including on trips, which nobody has ever explained to me. You didn’t have to pay for anything except the trips. You didn’t have to ask before leaving the room. You weren’t allowed to bring a phone into the building at all. But you could ask any question you liked, and that is the only rule I have kept.

speak.q: Answer out loud about your work or your studies: What do you have to do? What don’t you have to do? What aren’t you allowed to do? What can you do freely?
speak.model: I have to be at my desk by nine and I have to write a report every Friday. I don’t have to wear anything special. I’m not allowed to take work files home. I can work from home two days a week.
